recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core. Any future edits to the legal Questionnaire display-category or item-control codes should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack, not by restoring the removed core source files.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Questionnaire request to add a legal code to questionnaire-display-category and questionnaire-item-control so item-level copyright, trademark, patent, retention/use regulations, or other legal text can be represented as legal text instead of help text.
initial_application: Core commit 1893a91c27 added legal to source/questionnaire/codesystem-questionnaire-display-category.xml and source/questionnaire/codesystem-questionnaire-item-control.xml. Jira's only comment records that commit. Later core commits, including 17fa4f6e5e and 12b5e16b4a, adjusted neighboring display-category content and refined the legal display-category definition to say display text.
additional_context: Questionnaire remains active in source/fhir.ini, but the specific display-category and item-control code system/value set source files targeted by this issue are absent from current core. Commit dd468d4f17 removed the R5 extension artifacts from core. The local FHIR Extension Pack contains CodeSystem-questionnaire-display-category.xml and CodeSystem-questionnaire-item-control.xml, and both retain the legal code with definitions consistent with the approved issue and later terminology wording. Confluence SDC minutes for 2020-09-10 record FHIR-28363 as Persuasive with Modification, and no conflicting Zulip or Confluence FTS hits were found.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined core branch. No core files were changed because reintroducing retired core extension/terminology source would be incorrect; the authoritative current artifacts are in the Extension Pack and are already correct.

related_jiras.note: Later terminology cleanup changed display-category definitions, including legal, from generic text wording to display text wording. It explains the current definition difference from the original resolution prose.
A neighboring display-category issue removed the help display-category shortly after FHIR-28363 while leaving legal in place.
